title: Grader cards
description: Act three's four scoring programs, thirteen fields each, in both access states. Generated by scripts/build_grader_cards.py from the release bundle's rendered cards, its structured refusal records and its evidence records, all three cross-checked against each other. Consumed by components/grader-card on /see/grader/ section 3. NOT src/data/cards.json, which is the 27-row campaign ledger and is unrelated; pages/see-grader.md:48 cites both in one sentence. A refusal is a reading with a reason and a remedy, never a missing value, and a refusal whose remedy is empty fails the generator before it reaches the component.

fieldsPerCard.description: A card with fewer than this many fields fails the build naming the subject and the count.

fieldOrder.description: The order the library returns the fields in, identical on all four cards and in both access states. Readings and refusals are INTERLEAVED here and must render interleaved: sorting readings above refusals, or refusals behind a toggle, inverts the act. Recorded at the top so a renderer can assert its own order against it.

accessStates.description: Both states ship as data. The log-only state is a reachable state one control away from the default, not a hidden mode.

key.description: The bundle's own file key. A slug, not a public label.

displayName.description: The name the library renders. A third-party artifact name, so gate 7 must not fire on it.

kind.description: grader or environment. Two of each.

source.description: Where the program was read from, with its content hash. A local path on two of the four, because the framework was vendored; rendered as text and never as a link.

notes.description: The library's own notes on the subject, in the order it wrote them.

fingerprint.description: The content hash the card was built against. Two cards of the same program at different fingerprints describe two programs.

trust.description: The card's own trust level, computed by the gates rather than set by the caller. Rendered as a trust-badge.

evidenceId.description: The card's own record in the release bundle's evidence store.

graderCalls.description: A floor, not a total: the card's own cost line states how many of the fields that read do not model their own cost.

killedMutants.description: Zero on one subject and non-zero on the other three, which is what makes the zero a finding rather than a broken instrument.

bareHandlerCount.description: Bare `except:` handlers, each turning an internal failure into a verdict a caller cannot distinguish from a real one.

returns.description: What the handler returns instead of raising. This is the whole point of the census.

sourceLines.description: The denominator the handler count is read against.

bareHandlerEvidenceId.description: The handler census is its own record, so the count resolves separately from the card.

metamorphicApplicablePairs.description: The denominator, and it matters: applicable rollout-relation pairs, not rollouts. Zero on one subject, which is why the rate beside it is null rather than zero.

metamorphicViolationRate.description: Null where no pair was applicable. A null rate is not a rate of zero and must not render as one.

sensitiveFields.description: Fields whose reproducers the library withheld. Their headline is present and their payload is not, by a recorded disclosure decision.

log_only.description: The same card read by somebody holding only a log. THIS IS NOT UNIFORMLY ZERO READINGS: two of the four subjects still read `exploit-family accounting`, which is the one field countable from a log alone. components/grader-card.md:79 and its acceptance criterion 2 say every card drops to 0 of 13; the bundle says 0, 0, 1, 1, in both its rendered cards and its records. The repository wins and the contradiction is reported rather than smoothed.

byReason.description: Every key must be one of the seventeen in data/refusals.json. A reason outside the enum fails the build.

summarySentence.description: The library's own sentence about this state, rendered verbatim. On the emptied cards it reads that nothing was read so the card is a list of what it would take, which is the access argument in one line and is the library's wording rather than the site's.

reason.description: One of the seventeen, validated against data/refusals.json. Null on a reading.

detail.description: What was missing. The second of the four parts of a refusal.

remedy.description: What somebody would have to record to fill the field. Never empty on a refusal: the generator fails first, mirroring the library's own __post_init__ guard, and the component fails the build too.

bound.description: A floor rather than an estimate, where the refusal carries one.

headline.description: The library's sentence for a reading. Null on a refusal.

supporting.description: The reading's further lines, in order.

quantity.description: The registry id behind the field. An internal address: permitted here and on the registry route, banned from prose.
